t: Three Forces, One Stage, then Agam Band
x: Three Forces, One Stage, 6:30 to 7:30 PM: Harish Sivaramakrishnan, Sumanth Manjunath and Banjo Rancho bring together diverse sounds and traditions in a special musical collaboration. Harish Sivaramakrishnan is the lead vocalist and a founder member of the Bengaluru Carnatic progressive rock band Agam, and a playback singer in Malayalam, Tamil and Telugu cinema; in 2021 he won the SIIMA award for Best Playback Singer (Male) in Tamil for "Veyyon Silli" from Soorarai Pottru. Sumanth Manjunath is a violinist from Mysuru and Banjo Rancho is a drummer from Malta. Then Agam Band, 7:30 PM onwards: AGAM, the Carnatic Progressive Rock Experience, an acclaimed Bengaluru band that brings together the richness of Carnatic music and the energy of progressive rock. One ticket includes both shows.

Exploring rhythm, creativity and possibilities of the drum set. An engaging, fun and interactive workshop on the drum set, its history and evolution, and how it is used across musical styles and beyond music, in dance, theatre, film and sound effects. It looks at traditional and contemporary approaches, solo and group playing, composition and improvisation, with practical demonstrations and hands-on work on rhythmic patterns, stick techniques, coordination and practice methods. Open to everyone. No previous experience is necessary.

Discover the art of linocut printmaking in this hands-on creative workshop. Drawing inspiration from classical Indian dance mudras, rhythmic percussion patterns and traditional temple architecture, participants will sketch, carve and print their own unique designs. Learn basic carving techniques, explore textures and patterns, and create beautiful handmade prints on cotton rag paper to take home. No prior printmaking experience required.
Age: 18+
Duration: 2.5 hours
Prerequisites: None

pair: One ticket (includes this show and Mahabharata: A Mirror to Humanity)
x: The Making of an Epic Warrior. A Kalaripayattu performance by Atha Beyond that imagines how a warrior of the Mahabharata age would have trained, in body, mind and spirit: surrender to the guru, forging the body, one-pointed focus, mastery of weapons, and the warrior's code of knowing when not to strike. Told through authentic Kalari practice, with an oil lamp, live percussion and moments of silence. Continues straight into Mahabharata: A Mirror to Humanity, with no break between the two.
imgalt: Poster: The Warrior's Path, Kalaripayattu by Atha Beyond

t: Mahabharata: A Mirror to Humanity: The Dilemma of Dharma
w: Mallika Sarabhai, Dr. Lakshminarayan, Dr. Vasanth Kiran and Vyjayanthi Kashi
pair: One ticket (includes this show and The Warrior's Path)
x: The evening begins with The Warrior's Path at 7:00 PM and continues straight into Mahabharata, with no break between them. A captivating theatrical dance and movement experience exploring the untold stories, emotions and complexities of Ambe, Karna, Draupadi, Bheema and Duryodhana. Vyjayanthi Kashi as Ambe, Mallika Sarabhai as Draupadi, Dr. Lakshminarayan as Karna and Dr. Vasanth Kiran as Bheema bring the timeless epic to life through powerful storytelling and dance. 7:00 PM onwards in the Auditorium, after The Warrior's Path.
